app.stack: hybrid — Angular SPA in a WebView, crypto in assets/www JS (node-forge + JSEncrypt)

key.notes: 32 printable ASCII chars used as raw UTF-8 bytes (AES-256). Delivered by the two-step /app/init handshake, encrypted to the client's per-session RSA public key; the proxy-side patcher swaps that key for ours, decrypts the blob, appends '<ts>: <key> <session-id>' to the key log and re-encrypts to the app's real key. Renewed at 80% of the advertised exp, so one session owns several keys.

verified.how: captured body decrypted with the session's key; a re-encrypted body with a fresh random IV was accepted (200)

key.notes: same key as the request direction; the response body is a bare JSON string holding the token

notes: Non-standard JOSE: 5 segments with an EMPTY wrapped-key segment (the key is not in the message) and a single space as the tag segment — no authentication tag, so edits are accepted and the header's alg is cosmetic.
Plaintext is sometimes zlib-compressed as {"data":"<base64(deflate(json))>"} — crypto-cli.py inflates it automatically and --deflate produces it.

A second crypto model exists in the bundle (X25519 + HKDF → AES-GCM, header alg=X25519) behind a local config flag. If a captured header ever shows X25519, this whole profile is wrong — re-do steps 3–5.
The bundle also ships a hardcoded RSA-1024 keypair used by a separate helper (not the session crypto) — every install shares it; track the call sites and report it.
The proxy patcher only touches PROXY traffic: a handshake replayed from Repeater/MCP yields no key. Mint keys by restarting the app through the proxy, or run the handshake from a script.
Replays need HTTP/2 and the client's required headers (accept-language, app/session/correlation ids) — otherwise a transport rejection looks like a crypto failure.
